column1: # Player-facing settings: the iOS launcher (dm/ios/Sources/Launcher.swift) and the Mac app's settings window (dm/macos/Launcher.swift) show them before the game starts; Mac front ends read the same list.
# dm/games/settings.py writes one game's list into its app (dm/launcher.json): the rows whose condition holds for that game, with its defaults. Each sets an environment variable the host
# reads when the game starts. Columns, separated by tabs:
#   variable  the environment variable the setting sets
#   kind      choice: values value=label,... (languages: the game's own, from its control data); range: values low:high:step, shown as a percentage; toggle: 1 / 0 or <on>/<off>
#   default   a value; DM_GAME_<NAME>: the host's own default from the game profile (game_profile.h, game.py); build:<VAR>: the build's setting; <ios>|<mac>: per platform
#   shown     always; DM_GAME_<NAME>!=<value> or ==<value>; fixups:<KEY>: main's rewriter table has that key; languages>1; platform:mac / platform:ios; gfxapi:<api>
#   section   the heading on the settings screen: Game, Controls or Performance
#   label, note  the setting's name and the line under it (the note may be empty)
#   meta      extra keys, "key=value;...": level=basic (a front end shows it first), needs=<VAR>=<value> (a sub-setting, drawn only while <VAR> has that value)
# Rows the fork's host does not read (DM_PRESENT_SNAP, DM_PSO_MTL4, DM_PSO_PREBUILD, DM_RUMBLE_MIN, DM_UPSCALER, DM_SCREEN_ASPECT) are left out on purpose: a switch
# the host ignores would only sit in the window dead. FPS_TARGET/FPS_HOLD are always shown: DM_FPS_TARGET env is read by hle_fpslock.c even when the profile's own fps_target is 0.
